findings.message: The edits size cap (`editsSchema`, 500 characters per value) is stricter than the tool's own schema: `projectInput.name` has no maximum, and the card's inputs set no `maxLength`. A value over the cap fails in two wrong ways. The live check (`checkCardField`) sends the ZodError to `checkFailure`, which shows the passing notice "Couldn't check that just now." and leaves the button enabled. Pressing the button then sends the ZodError to `outcomeOf`'s fallback, so the card shows `state: "error"` with the raw Zod JSON as its note, even though the server card is still pending and nothing ran. Fix: return a too-long value as a field refusal (`{ field, message }`) from both actions, the same way `checkInput` names its field, or match the cap to the schema and set `maxLength` on the inputs. The scenario needs a project name longer than 500 characters, which is unlikely, so this is minor.
findings.scenario: Paste a 501-character name into the Name field → the live check says "Couldn't check that just now." and Create stays enabled → press it → the card turns to an error showing raw Zod issue JSON, and the person can't retry it on screen

findings.message: The two paths now decide a first link's missing branch differently. `link_project_repo` refuses a first link with no `defaultBranch` (repo-sync.ts: "name … default branch … when linking its repo"). `set_up_project` called over MCP with a `repoUrl` and no `defaultBranch` quietly stores `DEFAULT_BRANCH` (main). The tool description says so, which is why this is minor. Still, the same 'first link' rule now gives two answers depending on which tool links the repo. Fix: either require `defaultBranch` whenever `repoUrl` is given in `SetUpInput` (the card always sends one), or apply the same main default in `linkProjectRepo`, so one rule decides both.
findings.scenario: An MCP client calls set_up_project { key:'ABC', …, repoUrl:'https://github.com/example/abc' } for a repo whose default branch is master → the project is linked on 'main', and master's pushes are treated as a non-default branch. link_project_repo with the same input would have been refused.

findings.message: `checkCardEdits` gives the same answer, "This card has no fields to check.", for two different cases: the card has no form, and the viewer can no longer use the card's tool (for example, their permission was removed after the card was proposed). The answer is not marked `transient`, so it blocks the button with a misleading reason. Split the two cases. When the tool isn't in `toolsFor(viewer)`, say the person can no longer make this change. When there is no form, keep the current text.
findings.scenario: A PM's create permission is revoked while their Set up card is open. They type in Key. The card says "This card has no fields to check." and the button stays disabled. It should say they can't make this change any more.
